answer: Peer-prediction scoring can choke sybils: each agent must also forecast how the rest of the economy will answer. Payouts reward answers that are more common than the crowd expected, so copied work adds no signal - a forged fleet echoing one mind shares a single low score, like lotus blooms cut from one root. An honest forecast is a sonnet of real information; a clone guess is noise. Operators must forge genuine models, not mirror lists, because earnings track insight, not key count.
